title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-10
ranking_basis: Daily GitHub Trending star gains for ranks 1-10, with one separately labeled fresh-repository Search supplement
ranking_explanation: The 10 repositories from the matching daily Trending view are ordered by the displayed daily star-gain signal, descending. GestaltX is appended, not interleaved in that ranking: GitHub Search surfaced it among recently created and pushed repositories, but Search does not provide the matching daily star-gain figure.
global_caveat: Trending gains and current total-star counts are point-in-time measurements and can change during the day. The Search supplement's current stars are not a daily gain. No prior-window comparison was collected, so no Notable Shifts section is claimed. Project descriptions and performance statements are attributed to the repositories; no independent benchmark or safety audit was performed.

corroboration: GitHub REST API repository metadata and latest default-branch commit endpoints for all 11 listed repositories
Current GitHub README files for meta/astryx, sherlock-project/sherlock, anthropics/skills, mattpocock/skills, homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp, and vercel-labs/agent-browser

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-11-10 17:29 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-10 through 2026-11-10. Ranking basis: daily GitHub Trending star gains for the first ten entries, plus one separately labeled recent-repository Search supplement.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: AI-oriented developer tools dominate the strongest gains, led by Meta’s agent-ready Astryx design system (+3,111) and a wave of reusable agent skills. Browser and smart-home agent interfaces also have strong momentum, while Sherlock’s broad social-account search and established simulation software show interest beyond the agent ecosystem.

sections.title: meta/astryx
sections.content: An open-source, customizable design system built for developers and AI agents. Why notable: The day's largest reported gain; the README describes 150+ accessible components, theming, and a CLI designed to serve both people and agents.
sections.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready
sections.why_notable: The day's largest reported gain; its README describes 150+ accessible components, theming, and a CLI designed to serve both people and agents.
sections.unique_caveat: The README labels the project as currently in beta.

sections.title: sherlock-project/sherlock
sections.content: Finds public social-media accounts matching a username across 400+ networks. Why notable: A large one-day gain for an established, non-agent utility, showing today's interest is not confined to AI tooling.
sections.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks
sections.why_notable: A large one-day gain for an established, non-agent utility, suggesting today's interest is not confined to AI tooling.

sections.title: anthropics/skills
sections.content: A public collection of reusable Agent Skills and the associated specification. Why notable: Strong momentum around portable, task-specific instruction bundles, from examples to document and enterprise workflows.
sections.why_notable: Strong momentum around portable, task-specific instruction bundles, from examples to document and enterprise workflows.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.content: A collection of composable engineering skills for coding agents. Why notable: One of the largest gains; the README emphasizes small, editable, model-agnostic practices rather than a single end-to-end process framework.
sections.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
sections.why_notable: One of the largest gains; the README emphasizes small, editable, model-agnostic practices rather than a single end-to-end process framework.

sections.title: homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp
sections.content: An MCP server and Home Assistant integration for assistants to configure and automate a smart home. Why notable: Brings agent tooling into a real-world control domain through an in-process integration or server workflow.
sections.description: Configure and automate Home Assistant with Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI assistants.
sections.why_notable: Brings agent tooling into a real-world control domain, exposing a broad set of Home Assistant tools through an in-process integration or server workflow.

sections.title: vercel-labs/agent-browser
sections.content: A browser automation CLI that lets agents inspect pages and act through compact accessibility snapshots. Why notable: Its command-by-command loop, persistent browser session, and ref-based interaction make browser use an explicit agent tool workflow.
sections.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
sections.why_notable: Its command-by-command loop, persistent browser session, and ref-based interaction make browser use an explicit agent tool workflow.

sections.description: A collection of projects designed to help developers quickly get started with building deployable applications using the Claude API
sections.why_notable: Complements the skills trend with practical application scaffolding and deployable API examples.

sections.description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.

sections.title: google-deepmind/mujoco
sections.content: A general-purpose physics simulator for multi-joint dynamics with contact. Why notable: A current gain for mature simulation infrastructure provides a counterpoint to the day's software-agent concentration.
sections.description: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.
sections.why_notable: A current gain for mature simulation infrastructure provides a counterpoint to the day's software-agent concentration.

sections.title: ranxianglei/billion-context
sections.content: A context-compression plugin for long-running, token-intensive agent sessions. Why notable: Targets memory and context management for longer agent workflows; its efficiency figures are project claims, not independently benchmarked here.
sections.description: A context-compression plugin for month-long single sessions (billions of tokens), small context windows, and token savings.
sections.why_notable: Targets the memory and context-management bottleneck implied by longer agent workflows; its efficiency figures are project claims, not independently benchmarked here.
sections.unique_caveat: The claimed context duration and token savings were not independently benchmarked for this report.

sections.title: huamidev/GestaltX
sections.ranking_role: recent-search supplement; not ranked by daily Trending gains
sections.content: An iPhone and iPad MobileGestalt editor with device presets, backups, and plist tools. Why notable: Created 2026-11-09 and surfaced among the top-starred repositories created and pushed in the last two days; this is a Search signal, not a daily star-gain figure.
sections.description: An MobileGestalt editor for iOS 27.x, featuring region-code tweaks, device presets, backups, and support for 7 languages.
sections.why_notable: A GitHub Search supplement: it was created on 2026-11-09 and appeared among the highest-starred repositories created and pushed in the last two days. Current total stars are not treated as daily gains.
sections.unique_caveat: Its README says capability-flag effects depend on the device, OS version, and Apple services; supported on-device MobileGestalt access is listed for iOS/iPadOS 27.x.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Reusable skills for coding agents: anthropics/skills, mattpocock/skills, and addyosmani/agent-skills gained strongly, with claude-quickstarts as adjacent application scaffolding. Agent-to-tool use and longer sessions appear in ha-mcp, agent-browser, and billion-context. Astryx brings agent-ready components, themes, docs, and CLI into UI development. Sherlock and MuJoCo are non-agent-centered counterpoints; the fresh Search supplement GestaltX represents native iOS tooling. Languages: Python 4/11, TypeScript 2/11, Shell 1/11, JavaScript 1/11, Rust 1/11, C++ 1/11, Swift 1/11.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's strongest signal is the move from generic coding assistants toward practical agent ecosystems: portable skills, browser and smart-home tools, agent-aware interfaces, and context management. At the same time, gains for Sherlock and MuJoCo show that established utilities and technical infrastructure can still break through. The additional fresh-repository signal is noteworthy, but GitHub Search's current star count should not be mistaken for stars gained today.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily, retrieved 2026-11-10 at 17:29 UTC. Corroboration: GitHub REST API repository metadata and latest default-branch commits for all listed repos; GitHub Search API query created:2026-11-08..2026-11-10 pushed:2026-11-08..2026-11-10 stars:>100 identified GestaltX as a separate supplement. The first ten entries follow the daily Trending gains. GestaltX has no daily gain figure. README details were checked for main theme representatives. No prior-window comparison was available, so Notable Shifts is omitted.
